title: Space/join invite-uses increment is non-atomic with member-add: lost increments + uses-exhaustion failures
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:1335-1515 (handle_space_join invite path).

Two distinct race issues:

(1) Lost increment / partial commit:
- Line 1336: new_uses = invite.uses.saturating_add(1) — computed BEFORE membership write.
- Line 1426-1434: membership write via update_object<Space>.
- Line 1503-1515: invite uses update_object<SpaceInvite> with new_uses — runs AFTER membership write.
If step 2 succeeds and step 3 fails (backend transient, restart, etc.), the member is added but uses never increments. An attacker can:
 - share an invite,
 - force step-3 failures by triggering backend errors,
 - and have unlimited members join via what was meant to be a single-use invite.

The two writes are not in a single transaction; the kit's design assumes the backend can recover, but the reference MemoryBackend has no rollback path and the trait does not require atomicity.

(2) Stale new_uses overwrites concurrent increments:
- Caller A reads uses=5, plans to write 6.
- Caller B reads uses=5, plans to write 6.
- Both write 6. The maxUses=10 invite has effectively been used twice but the counter only reflects one use. With high concurrency, a maxUses=N invite can admit far more than N members.

Fix sketch:
- Make invite-uses increment server-atomic. Either:
  (a) wrap both writes in a single backend.apply_join_invite call (new trait method), or
  (b) use a compare-and-swap primitive: update SpaceInvite with 'expected uses=5, new uses=6', backend rejects if uses no longer 5. Caller retries.
- Re-order so the invite uses increment happens FIRST (atomic CAS); only proceed to membership add if increment succeeded. That way over-counting is impossible and under-counting only occurs on cleanup failures (where the invite is consumed but membership fails — still bounded by maxUses).

Trigger: any production deployment with >1 user attempting to join via the same invite code concurrently, OR any deployment where the second update_object call can fail.
close_reason: Fixed in a9856984: required ChatBackend::join_space_with_invite (atomic check+member add+uses increment); tests/space_join_invite_atomic.rs (3). Cross-account last-use race not modellable in MemoryBackend (per-account storage); covered by trait contract.
